tasks.short: Maintain attendance and approved grade records

steps.what: Capture attendance and reconcile examiner-approved grades against the student roster
Copy verified attendance and grades into the required second record system
Resolve record mismatches and approve publication of the final student records

tasks.design: Configure a native {LMS} export into the student records system represented by {OTHER}. Stage verified rows, reconcile totals and retain the teacher's publication decision.
tasks.enabler_now: A supported import can map existing identifiers and approved values.
tasks.still_hard: Student identity conflicts, changed grades and missing sessions need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher establishes attendance and checks the academic record.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry; academic decision rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: The digest documents a requirement to publish grades in both Brightspace and OSIRIS, establishing a possible duplicate-entry boundary rather than a measured saving.
A supported staged import could remove repeat entry while preserving capture and publication checks; the labour estimates are scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is record maintenance, excluding marking and examiner decisions; existing examiner grade approval remains unchanged upstream.

In s1 the teacher produces student ID, course ID, session date, attendance code, assessment ID, approved grade and source version; all capture and reconciliation time remains in its 40 hours. Missing identifiers or unsupported values use manual entry in s3.
Test native configuration first. OTHER denotes the student records system. Already automated transfers earn no additional saving.
unknowns: Whether a second manual entry actually occurs
research_questions: Does an observed record batch reconcile fully after a staged native import?

tasks.short: Revise literature curricula and teaching methods

steps.what: Evaluate curricula, student work and course feedback to choose revision priorities
Draft revised course materials and methods from the agreed curriculum priorities

loop.input: Teacher's revision brief and selected source materials
loop.output: Revision draft linked to outcomes and sources
loop.check: Teacher checks interpretation, coverage, teaching sequence and fidelity to each source passage
loop.stop: One revision attempt; unsupported passages or poor teaching fit are rewritten manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Selecting pedagogically useful wording and examples requires interpretation

steps.what: Check the revised curriculum and adopt the final course materials

tasks.design: Keep evaluation and revision priorities with the teacher in {DOCS}. A bounded draft uses only supplied materials, and the teacher checks and adopts the final revision in {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Revision drafting repeatedly restates existing material.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting tool can work against a teacher-authored brief.
tasks.still_hard: Literary interpretation and curriculum balance require subject expertise.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher decides which intellectual challenges students should encounter.
tasks.altitude: More time evaluating student understanding; no new curriculum approval authority.

evidence.claim: Teacher-reviewed drafting from selected curriculum materials is plausible; no curriculum-development time study supports these estimates.

assumptions: Boundary is one teacher's course revision, excluding institution-wide programme approval.

Teacher produces outcome IDs, revision goals, selected passages, source editions and teaching constraints in s1; its full 45 hours includes this preparation. Missing context goes to manual drafting in s2.
Test existing document tools and templates before a model add-on; never infer student grades or ability from feedback.
research_questions: Do draft revisions meet the teacher's priorities without adding correction time?

incremental.description: Maintain draft instructions and inspect recurring errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact curriculum revision, selected readings, learning outcomes and teaching methods; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=45+21+20=86; gross 14 less 4 upkeep gives net 10. Low assumes native templates suffice and no model rollout; high requires 40% less drafting time without shorter evaluation.

steps.what: Prepare lecture arguments, quotations and examples about poetry, novels or translation
Format prepared lecture content into slides and teaching notes
Check the presentation and deliver lectures with discussion and close reading

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} layouts to format teacher-authored lecture sections and exact quotations. The teacher checks the output before teaching and retains all interpretation, classroom interaction and delivery time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual presentation formatting consumes preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable layouts can render already structured lecture content.
tasks.still_hard: A faithful quotation is not automatically a useful interpretation or lesson.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher performs close reading and responds to students' interpretations.
tasks.altitude: Less layout work; teaching and scholarly decisions stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native layouts can format teacher-authored lecture content; the preparation share and resulting savings are unmeasured scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is lecture preparation and delivery, excluding separate curriculum revision.

Teacher produces section order, headings, exact text, quotation editions, page references and image permissions in s1, whose full 35 hours includes structuring. Missing fields or unsuitable layouts are corrected manually in s3.
Test native layouts first. No generated literary claims; no saving on research, interpretation, student discussion or existing system runtime.
research_questions: Can a representative lecture render without moving content-authoring work into extra form filling?

already_counted.description: Content authoring and structured input capture

incremental.description: Maintain accessible layouts and test rendered quotations

approvals.approved_version: Exact rendered presentation and teaching notes checked before delivery; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80; gross 20 less 4 upkeep gives net 16. Low assumes reusable slides already remove layout effort and no change is deployed; high requires the full observed 20-hour formatting share.

tasks.short: Give extra coursework help outside class

steps.what: Assist students with coursework through questions, close reading and guided practice

tasks.design: Retain the teacher's individual help, using the coursework already available in {LMS} when needed. No additional intake or automated tutoring step is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficulty must be understood through dialogue.
tasks.enabler_now: None changes the need for personal teaching in this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: A student's confidence or interpretation can change during the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher notices misunderstanding and adjusts the explanation.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in this task's decision rights or weekly effort.

evidence.claim: Individual coursework help remains a teacher-led interaction; no additional administrative baseline is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the help conversation, excluding booking and separately assessed grading.
